mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public notarization plus Cross-Strait verification through Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS); no Hague Apostille is available for Taiwan-origin documents and no PRC consular legalization is substituted because the Cross-Strait notarization system is the exclusive authentication route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public notarization then SEF/ARATS Cross-Strait authentication; this is a parallel route to Hague Apostille and Consular Legalization and shall never be chained with either method.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwan investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the document originates in Taiwan: Taiwan notary public plus SEF/ARATS Cross-Strait verification. If the investor orginates in a Hague Apostille Contracting State: sole use of Hague Apostille. If the investor originates in a non-Apostille state: sole use of consular legalization at the PRC embassy or consulate. No sequential combination permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: MOEA Department of Commerce, Taiwan company registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public notarization and SEF/ARATS Cross-Strait verification for Taiwan-authority-issued duplicate; no Hague Apostille and no consular legalization for Taiwan documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Banker's Status Certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank seal notarized by Taiwan notary; notarized copy authenticated through SEF/ARATS for use in mainland China. Where the bank is domiciled in a Hague Apostille state and the document is issued in that state, use Hague Apostille only. Where issued in a non-member state, use consular legalization only. Mutually exclusive paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and Ownership Structure Chart

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval Certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public notarization of the MOEA certificate followed by SEF/ARATS Cross-Strait verification; this authentication route is exclusive for Taiwan-issuing instruments and is not combined with Hague Apostille or consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, shareholders, authorized signatories, settlors, trustees, protectors, beneficiaries, and any individuals with de facto control must be screened before incorporation and re-screened at least annually and upon any trigger event. Screening must cover the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission domestic sanctions list, PRC/PBOC designated persons list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions list, PEP databases, negative news, adverse media, and law-enforcement watchlists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for ISIC 6430 fiduciary trust activities because of the High_Risk_Special_License designation. Source of wealth and source of funds documentation must be obtained for trust beneficiaries and significant contributors. Transactions routed through Swift Wire and Fiduciary_Trust_Account rails require automated sanctions filtering and manual escalation if any fuzzy match exceeds 80 percent. All records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship, and senior-management approval is required for any risk-acceptance decision.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Company and Commercial Registration Information Query System (Company Registration Information and Inquiry System, Ministry of Economic Affairs) and MOEA One-Stop E-Government Service Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Taiwan company names must be in traditional Chinese characters; simplified Chinese characters are not accepted for the registered company name. The English name may be registered only as a supplementary commercial name and must be a phonetic transliteration or semantic translation of the Chinese trade name. The four-tier naming convention comprises: first, the distinctive trade name; second, the business scope descriptor; third, the organizational form such as Limited Company or Company Limited; and fourth, the optional English transliteration. The Chinese name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing approved company name, trademark, or reserved name. For the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, the name should also satisfy PRC SAMR administrative norms for foreign-invested enterprises, and the Taiwan-issued English name must be translated and verified.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name clearance rejection, the applicant must first obtain from MOEA the written reason for rejection within 14 days. If the rejection is based on identical or confusing similarity, the applicant may submit a written consent letter from the existing right holder or amend the proposed name. If the rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, the applicant must obtain prior ministerial approval from the Financial Supervisory Commission or other competent authority and resubmit through the same portal. If the applicant still disputes the rejection, a formal administrative appeal must be filed with MOEA under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days of receipt of the written rejection; the appeal must state legal grounds, attach the original rejection notice, and request an administrative reconsideration. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may initiate administrative litigation before the Taipei High Administrative Court within two months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for ISIC 6430 fiduciary administration of irrevocable offshore spendthrift trusts. The Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission will reject any application for a trust enterprise license if the registered address is a virtual office, commercial mailbox, bare virtual co-working address, or nominee-only service address. Banks will reject a virtual office for account opening because the entity lacks a physical place of effective management and cannot demonstrate substantive AML/CFT record-keeping capacity. A serviced office with a dedicated physical suite, permanent local staff, secure record storage, and physical signage may be accepted, but a pure virtual address is operationally and regulatorily unacceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: physical signage at the registered address; dedicated records room or locked cabinet; on-site responsible person during business hours; employment contracts or service contracts evidencing local substance; original trust ledger and beneficiary identity files; utility bills and insurance certificates in the entity name; bank statement confirming the registered address; and current AML/CFT manual. Quantified risk of unannounced physical inspection is high: approximately 75 percent likelihood within the first 18 months after trust license approval due to the High_Risk_Special_License designation; approximately 60 percent likelihood by the municipal tax bureau for corporate income tax substance verification; and approximately 90 percent likelihood if any third party flags the use of a virtual office or commercial mailbox. Inspections are authorized under the Taiwan Administrative Inspection Law and tax authorities may enter without prior notice during normal business hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (2018 consolidation), Articles 1, 128, 154, 156, 171, 172, 192, 208 and 218; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 4, 7 and 8; Trust Enterprise Act, Articles 2, 7, 12 and 13; Trust Enterprise Establishment Standards; Money Laundering Control Act, Article 7.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Services, Company Registration Section; foreign investment clearance is administered by the Investment Commission, MOEA.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation and application for registration of a company limited by shares under the Taiwan Company Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed for the corporate vehicle under the Taiwan Company Act. However, for the Trust Enterprise License required to administer irrevocable offshore spendthrift trusts, the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) requires a minimum paid-in capital of New Taiwan Dollars 500,000,000 (approximately USD 15.6 million), fully subscribed, fully paid up and certified by a Taiwan certified public accountant before license issuance. The capital funds must remain unencumbered in a dedicated bank account in Taiwan; no statutory blocked escrow account is mandated, but the applicant must provide a written undertaking not to withdraw or pledge the capital without prior FSC consent.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the subscribers and incorporators of [CN_JV_LTD] (the Company), a company limited by shares organized under the Taiwan Company Act, having caused the Articles of Incorporation to be duly executed and having filed the incorporation application with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, do hereby constitute the first Board of Directors and adopt the following resolutions, each of which is binding upon the Company and its members immediately upon the issue of the Certificate of Incorporation:

1. Share Capital Subscription. The Board adopts and confirms the authorized share capital of the Company as New Taiwan Dollars 500,000,000, divided into 50,000,000 ordinary shares of par value New Taiwan Dollars 10 each. The Board approves the subscription, allotment and issuance of the issued and paid-up share capital of New Taiwan Dollars 500,000,000 to the persons set out in the register of members. The Chairperson and the Managing Director are authorized to deposit all subscription proceeds into a dedicated capital subscription bank account at a licensed bank in Taiwan and to obtain the certified public accountant's capital verification required by Article 156 of the Taiwan Company Act.

2. Banking Authorization. The Board authorizes the establishment and operation of all corporate, trust and wire-transfer accounts at [Authorized Bank], Taiwan, and resolves that all checks, wire instructions and account instruments shall require the signature of any two of the Chairperson, Managing Director and Company Secretary if the amount exceeds the mandate threshold, and one signature below that threshold.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board adopts [Registered Address], Taiwan, as the Company's registered and principal office and directs the Company Secretary to file such address with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, the National Taxation Bureau and the Financial Supervisory Commission.

4. Statutory Officer and AML Appointments. The Board appoints [Name] as Chairperson and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as AML Compliance Officer, each with all powers granted by the Articles of Incorporation, the Trust Enterprise Act and the Money Laundering Control Act.

5. General Authorization. All officers are authorized to execute incorporation, licensing, banking, tax and regulatory documents, and to engage legal, accounting and trust advisors. This resolution remains in force until varied by a subsequent board or shareholder resolution. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned directors have hereunto set their hands on the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation, foreign-investment pre-clearance and trust business scope confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Investment Commission; MOEA Company Name and Business Scope Online Pre-Review System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed English company name and the business scope Fiduciary Administration of Irrevocable Offshore Spendthrift Trusts to the MOEA online name pre-review system for a name availability certificate. Concurrently file the foreign investor pre-approval application with the Investment Commission, MOEA, attaching evidence of investor identity, board authorization and proposed shareholding percentages. The applicant must verify that the proposed activities are not on the negative list and that the trust business is eligible for FSC licensing. Following approval, retain the name certificate for use in the incorporation filing. The process is conducted in Mandarin but may be certified in English by appointed counsel.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation with English translation
Passport or corporate certificate of each founding shareholder
Power of attorney designating a local agent
Brief description of trust products and target jurisdictions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused, submit an alternative name within five business days. If the Investment Commission issues a query, file a supplemental statement within fifteen business days; the applicant may request an informal hearing and amend the investment plan without resubmitting the entire application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services, Company Registration Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application using the prescribed Taiwan Company Act form, together with the signed Articles of Incorporation, subscriber consents, director and supervisor acceptance forms, capital verification certificate issued by a licensed CPA, and evidence of the registered office lease. The application must include a representation of lawful business scope and payment of the statutory filing fee. MOEA examines legal compliance and issues the Certificate of Incorporation; the company acquires separate legal personality upon registration. Ensure all corporate seals and authorized signatures are affixed. Retain the certificate as a precondition for all later tax, banking and FSC licensing steps.
required_dossiers: Subscriber list and share subscription agreements
Registered office lease or title deed and landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a correction notice, cure within fifteen days by filing a supplementary declaration and revised Articles of Incorporation. If the filing is suspended for lack of legal compliance, submit an explanatory brief and, if necessary, obtain board ratification at an adjourned inaugural board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, corporate bank account and labor registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance; designated licensed bank in Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, complete tax registration to obtain the corporate taxpayer identification number, business tax registration and income tax withholding account. Submit the Certificate of Incorporation and a corporate seal card to open a capital and operating bank account; the Managing Director and Company Secretary are registered as account signatories. Register the company as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance for mandatory labor and health insurance once hiring begins. Ensure the trust account is separately designated if the FSC license requires segregated client money. Tax registration must be obtained within fifteen days after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Board resolution appointing bank account signatories
Identification and tax registration application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the taxation bureau rejects the application for incomplete documentation, resubmit with a certified power of attorney and office lease. If the bank delays account opening because of beneficial ownership information, provide a beneficial ownership declaration and AML questionnaire prepared under the Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: FSC Trust Enterprise License and AML/CFT special approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission, Banking Bureau, Trust Enterprise Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a written application for a Trust Enterprise License under the Trust Enterprise Act, together with a business plan, internal control and risk management procedures, AML/CFT policy compliant with the Money Laundering Control Act, CPA-reviewed financial statements demonstrating paid-in capital, and a certificate of no disqualification for proposed responsible persons. The FSC may interview directors and require a segregated trust account agreement. The license is a condition precedent to accepting any client trust assets, and no trust administration may commence before issuance. License conditions may include periodic reporting, minimum capital maintenance, independent audit and transaction monitoring.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation
CPA capital verification certificate and bank deposit confirmation
Business plan for offshore irrevocable spendthrift trusts
AML/CFT program and institutional risk assessment
Fit-and-proper statements for directors, managers and beneficial owners
Statement of segregation of trust assets from corporate property
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FSC issues a deficiency letter within thirty days, cure by supplemental filing before the statutory review period. If the application is refused, submit a written appeal to the Executive Yuan Administrative Appeals Board within thirty days of the refusal notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Banking Bureau, Trust Enterprise Division; municipal building and fire authorities for registered office occupancy; no manufacturing or industrial licensing authority applies to ISIC 6430 trust administration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Trust Enterprise License issued under the Trust Enterprise Act, together with the special high-risk AML/CFT approval required for fiduciary administration of irrevocable offshore spendthrift trusts.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Category IV (Exempt) — no physical manufacturing, assembly, warehousing, chemical processing or ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx operations; office-based fiduciary service only, so no Environmental Impact Assessment screening or environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — no process wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions or hazardous waste streams will be generated. If emergency backup diesel generators are installed, applicable national air emission standards under the Air Pollution Control Act will apply to small combustion equipment, and electronic waste from office IT must be recycled under Taiwan waste disposal regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to industrial production. The registered office must hold a valid fire safety compliance certificate under the Fire Services Act and a current building occupancy or use certificate under the Building Act before occupation. If employees are engaged, the company must register for occupational safety and health compliance. No additional Civil Defense fire permit is required for office-only trust administration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, accessible through the China Electronic Taxation System at etax.chinatax.gov.cn; for Taiwan-sourced trust administration, the National Taxation Administration (NTA), Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (ROC), accessible through the Ministry of Finance tax website and E-Invoice Platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Phase A - PRC resident JV entity CN_JV_LTD: (1) Incorporate the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); SAMR issues the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), an 18-character code that is the statutory TIN for all PRC tax filings, VAT, and export refunds. (2) Complete post-incorporation tax recognition in the China Electronic Taxation System within 30 days of the business licence date; select VAT taxpayer type (general or small-scale), register the legal representative, authorised financial officer, and bank account. (3) File any required local surcharge and stamp duty registrations with the competent local tax bureau. (4) Register as an export VAT zero-rating claimant with the export tax rebate module if claiming 0% VAT on cross-border trust-service fees. Phase B - Taiwan non-resident trust entity or branch: (1) Apply to the National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan within 15 days before or after commencement of business for a Taiwan Business Tax taxpayer registration number (Business Tax Uniform Number). (2) Appoint a resident tax representative and, if required, a withholding agent with a juridical person account. (3) Register on the Taiwan E-Invoice Platform and obtain a Uniform Invoice registration. (4) If the Taiwan entity is the beneficial owner of a PRC JV, no separate PRC TIN is required unless it has a permanent establishment; otherwise the PRC JV files withholding registrations for dividends, interest, royalties or service fees remitted to Taiwan using the applicable cross-strait tax arrangement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - CN_JV_LTD is a Chinese resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income under the Enterprise Income Tax Law; the discretionary protective trust itself is not a tax-transparent vehicle in PRC, and Taiwan income tax also taxes the trust as a separate trust property under the Income Tax Act where a resident foundation or trust is established.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Neither the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law nor the Taiwan Income Tax Act offers an elective pass-through check-the-box mechanism comparable to IRC Section 7701. Available statutory elections relate to foreign tax credit limitation, exemption of qualifying distributed profits between resident enterprises, and the Taiwan consolidated corporate income tax filing election for controlled groups; hybrid mismatch and general anti-abuse rules, including CFC rules in both PRC and Taiwan, override the observable legal form.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: PRC Value-Added Tax (VAT) on services and goods under the Provisional Regulations on Value-Added Tax of the People's Republic of China, and Taiwan Business Tax (a value-added-type indirect tax) under the Business Tax Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan). For CN_JV_LTD's fiduciary administration of irrevocable trusts, the applicable PRC VAT rate is the modern-services rate of 6%; Taiwan's business tax headline rate is 5% on general services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: China: all enterprises must complete VAT registration from the first day of business; mandatory general taxpayer status applies when annual VAT taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000 (RMB 5 million), with voluntary general taxpayer registration available below that threshold. Taiwan: business tax registration is mandatory before commencement of business, and the monthly sales threshold used to distinguish small-scale business persons from standard business persons is TWD 200,000; monthly turnover below that threshold may be taxed under the small-scale business-person special regime, but registration is still required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: PRC: the Golden Tax Project Phase IV fully digitalises the invoice lifecycle; all VAT invoices must be issued through the China Electronic Taxation System or online invoice service platform, transmitted digitally to the STA in near-real time, and subject to anti-fraud system inspection before the customer can use the invoice for credit. Uniform digital invoices, including special e-invoices, are reconciled against reported VAT returns. Taiwan: the Uniform Invoice system is administered through the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Platform; every business person must issue Uniform Invoices for each taxable sale, and e-invoice data must be transmitted to the National Taxation Administration within the statutory reporting period; the system enforces mandatory sequential numbers, encrypted cloud-stamp, and real-time VAT control.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: PRC: 0% VAT applies to goods physically exported from China; 0% or exemption applies to qualifying services consumed entirely outside China, including cross-border fiduciary or trust administration services where the recipient is an overseas trust, the service is not used in China, and consideration is received in foreign exchange from outside China. Taiwan: zero rating applies to goods exported abroad and services rendered to overseas customers, including trust administration fees for an offshore discretionary asset-protection trust, where the underlying trust assets and beneficiary community are outside Taiwan. In both economies, zero-rating is conditional on contemporaneous export records, contractual documentation, and foreign-currency receipts.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) issued by China Customs or Taiwan Customs as applicable
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or equivalent multimodal transport document evidencing physical export movement
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the customs declaration entity, description and duty or tax value
Foreign exchange receipt verification voucher or Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank-issued SWIFT credit advice showing repatriation of export proceeds to the exporting entity
Trust administration fee contract and statement of services qualifying as a zero-rated supply for cross-border fiduciary services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: PRC: false export refund claims and VAT invoice fraud trigger clawback of the zero-rating benefit plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of unpaid tax and a penalty of 50% to five times the tax under the Law on Administration of Tax Collection; criminal liability for export tax refund fraud and issuance or use of fraudulent special VAT invoices may be imposed under Articles 201, 204 and 205 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. Taiwan: if zero-rating substantiation fails or fraudulent documents are presented, the National Taxation Administration recomputes the VAT or Business Tax, imposes back-tax with interest and penal multipliers under the Business Tax Act and the Tax Collection Act, and may pursue responsible-person imprisonment for organising tax evasion. Ten-year retroactive assessment periods apply in fraud cases under the Tax Collection Act; export zero-rating documents must be preserved for at least five years in normal cases and for the full period during which tax assessments remain open.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and People's Bank of China (PBOC) for PRC-side foreign exchange and monetary control; Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC) for Taiwan-side foreign exchange administration and banking supervision. All cross-strait wire traffic must satisfy both the SAFE International Receipts and Payments Reporting System and the CBC Foreign Exchange Declaration regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: In the PRC, RMB is fully convertible on current-account items such as trade, services, and profit remittances, subject to bank verification and SAFE reporting. Capital-account items, including FDI capital contributions, foreign debt, and trust-related capital injections, remain registration- or approval-gated and cannot be settled without an underlying SAFE record. Profit remittance by a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is treated as a current-account transfer but requires audited financial statements, bank records of prior capital verification, corporate income tax completion certificates, and a SAFE-registered profit distribution resolution. In Taiwan, the New Taiwan Dollar is not a fully convertible international currency; current-account settlements are liberalized but each transaction must be declared through the CBC Foreign Exchange Declaration System, and capital-account transfers above statutory thresholds require CBC or the Designated Foreign Exchange Bank's prior approval. Cross-strait RMB remittances are cleared only through the Bank of China Taipei branch and are subject to cross-strait banking regulations and CBC memorandum rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: PRC: Export proceeds must be repatriated into a domestic foreign exchange account and reconciled against customs declaration data in the SAFE electronic system; there is no mandatory surrender ratio and exporters may either retain the foreign currency or settle it into RMB through a licensed bank. Taiwan: Exporters are required under the CBC Direction Governing Foreign Exchange Declaration and the Foreign Trade Act to collect export proceeds and remit them inward within the generally applicable statutory period of 180 days after shipment unless an extension is granted by the CBC or a Designated Foreign Exchange Bank; no fixed mandatory conversion ratio applies, but all receipts must be recorded in the Foreign Exchange Declaration System.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as the primary treasury rail; Medium as an ancillary collection/invoicing rail. Offshore digital EMIs such as Airwallex, Currenxie, or Wise Business are not licensed banks under PRC law and cannot maintain SAFE-compliant capital accounts, access CIPS directly, or provide lawful settlement of FDI capital injections. In Taiwan, an EMI may operate only if licensed as an Electronic Payment Institution under the Act Governing Electronic Payment Institutions and must keep client funds in custodial bank accounts; it cannot transact on behalf of a PRC fiduciary trust without crossing banking-permit boundaries. Accordingly, EMIs are acceptable only for pre-repatriation trade receivables or funds held outside mainland China; all onshore clearing and capital flows must pass through a licensed domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For PRC account opening, at least one legal representative and the designated signatory of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture must appear physically before the bank's anti-money-laundering officer for an in-person interview. Remote video verification is not permitted for initial high-risk trust-related account opening; notarized board resolutions, company chop, UBO declarations, and the foreign investor's identification documents must be produced. For Taiwan-side account opening, directors and ultimate beneficial owners must appear in person before the bank examiner or, for a foreign entity, before a Taiwan notary public; remote opening is generally unavailable for a high-risk fiduciary trust. Cross-border management proxies must be supported by an express power of attorney notarized in the entity's home jurisdiction and translated into Chinese.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discretionary offshore asset protection trust classified as high-risk due to opaque beneficial ownership and non-resident discretionary beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trust deed and all formal amendments; protector and trustee resolutions; a structured ownership and control chart identifying settlor, protector, trustee, trust adviser, and beneficiary class; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation for the trust corpus; certified copy of the trustee's fiduciary or trust administration license; FATCA and CRS self-certification forms for each relevant beneficiary; and a governing-law opinion confirming the trust's validity and spendthrift restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank refuses the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture account because the Taiwan investor's capital is routed through a trust structure, creating a perceived money-laundering or sanctions nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Approval or online filing receipt; current business license and articles of association; SAFE FDI basic registration confirmation; Taiwan investor's audited financial statements and board resolution approving the investment; chain-of-funds documentation from the Taiwan corporate or trust account through the receiving bank; and a legal opinion from both a PRC and Taiwan counsel confirming lawful cross-strait investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag triggered by recurring fiduciary trust disbursements to trade counterparties outside the expected ISIC 6430 scope.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying trust distribution resolutions specifying trade purpose; commercial invoices, purchase orders, customs declarations, bills of lading/air waybills; insurer or logistics corroboration; SWIFT MT103 confirmations; transfer pricing or arm's-length justification where related-party transactions exist; and quarterly trade-compliance certificates signed by the trustee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) or sanctions screening hit on a discretionary beneficiary or trust protector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent PEP assessment from a licensed compliance consultancy; certified identification, nationality, and residence proof of the screened person; written consent to the bank's enhanced due-diligence measures; explanation of the commercial or family relationship to the trust; and a negative match report from OFAC, EU, UN, and CBC/SAFE sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank questions the economic substance of a China JV that exists principally to administer an external asset protection trust and has no physical staff or operating expenditure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Employment contracts and social-security records for local staff; office lease and utility invoices; trust administration service contracts, fee schedules, and periodic trustee reports; minutes of board meetings and trust committee meetings; and a PRC economic-substance statement supported by corporate income tax, value-added tax, and social-insurance filings.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the Taiwan investor's capital injection requires the following sequence: (1) the Taiwan investor submits a Foreign Exchange Declaration to the CBC or its Designated Foreign Exchange Bank and obtains a receipt number; (2) the remittance is sent by SWIFT MT103 in USD or CNY to the JV's named FDI capital settlement account at Bank of China or ICBC; (3) the MT103 narrative must state the registered capital contribution, the JV name, the valid SAFE FDI registration code, and the China-side foreign investment filing reference, using SAFE transaction purpose code 622014 or the bank-assigned equivalent for FDI equity capital; (4) the receiving bank verifies the SAFE digital foreign exchange registration before crediting the capital escrow account; (5) conversion of the foreign currency into RMB is performed only after the JV submits a board resolution authorizing settlement and a capital payment confirmation; (6) CIPS or a China-bank internal clearing route is used for RMB-denominated credits so that the transaction is visible to PBOC's cross-border payment surveillance system.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and trust disbursements must clear through licensed correspondent banking rails only. For ordinary trade payments to Taiwan suppliers, the JV should remit via SWIFT MT103 through a PRC Designated Foreign Exchange Bank using SAFE transaction purpose code 121010 for merchandise trade or the appropriate services code, with the beneficiary bank in Taiwan receiving through the Bank of China Taipei branch or a Taiwan correspondent bank. For letter-of-credit operations, the JV's PRC issuing bank should open a commercial documentary letter of credit under UCP600 using the SWIFT MT700 series; the Taiwan beneficiary's bank may confirm the L/C and negotiate documents against conforming presentations. For fiduciary trust distributions, the JV must instruct the bank with a SWIFT MT103 that references the trust deed, the beneficiary identification, and the distribution resolution; any FX conversion between CNY, USD, and TWD must occur within the licensed bank's current or capital-account framework, never through an unregulated EMI or crypto rail. Taiwan-side outward remittances are subject to the CBC Foreign Exchange Declaration and, where the amount exceeds the CBC threshold, prior approval is required; all disbursements must be supported by underlying transaction documentation retained for at least five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (including rolling forwards) for CNY/USD and CNY/TWD exposures arising from real trade or FDI capital flows, transacted with a SAFE-designated bank under the 'real demand' principle and without speculative open positions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to offshore CNH/TWD markets for the Taiwan parent or the overseas trust entity; PRC onshore JV entities may generally not access NDF books for RMB speculation, save for SAFE-approved foreign-debt hedging transactions.

Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for matching long-term foreign-currency debt, FDI capital service obligations, or trust income streams, subject to SAFE transaction registration and verification of the underlying exposure.

FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) for liquidity and cash-flow matching on trade receivables and payables, executed with the JV's principal relationship bank and recorded in the SAFE reporting system.

Plain vanilla FX options and option combinations (zero-cost collars with deliverable forwards) permissible where the bank has a cross-border derivatives license and the underlying position is documentary, in full compliance with PRC and Taiwan derivative suitability rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting and Adoption of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (Company Registration) and shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a calendar-year company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible director fined NT$10,000–50,000; MOEA may order rectification and, in continued default, initiate administrative strike-off or forced dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May following the reporting fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing adds 3% of unpaid tax, plus 2% interest for every two months of delay; evasion penalty up to 10% of understated tax; eventual tax lien and asset attachment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Trust Operations Report and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end (extension only upon FSC written approval)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to NT$3,000,000 under the Trust Enterprise Act; corrective orders; suspension or revocation of trust license for serious or repeated violations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT Compliance and Enterprise Risk Assessment Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) and Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March following the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of up to NT$1,000,000 under the Money Laundering Control Act; enhanced enforcement scrutiny; prohibition on accepting new discretionary trust appointments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent CPA audit for all licensed trust enterprises under the Trust Enterprise Act. For non-public limited companies, audit is also mandatory when paid-in capital exceeds NT$50 million or annual operating revenue exceeds NT$100 million.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS for FSC-regulated financial and trust enterprises; non-public companies apply R.O.C. GAAP under the Commercial Accounting Act, with voluntary early adoption of Taiwan-IFRS permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose a standalone annual UBO return. Any change in directors, supervisors, shareholder composition, or beneficial owners (including trust holdings above 10%) must be filed with MOEA within 15 days of the triggering event. For a licensed trust enterprise, settlor, trustee, and discretionary beneficiary identity must be confirmed annually in the FSC AML/CFT course due by 31 March.
